items.storyText:
Look at the classroom. These are your new tables and chairs.

Those are your new pegs. Animal pegs!

That is our new whiteboard. And this is the new computer. Look! Wow!

Do you like our new things? Yes, we do.

And is this a new teddy, Rosy? No …

This is my new pencil case. Look, new pencils and pens!

When I'm really sad, I cry and tell my mum. We always talk together, then happy times can come. When I'm really nervous, I'm brave and carry on. I say, 'I can do it!' until my nerves are gone. Sometimes I am happy. Sometimes I am sad. Sometimes I am nervous. But I am never bad.

items.title: Unit 2 · Lesson 1 story
items.storyText:
Hello, babies! They're twins – brother and sister.

Oh no. They're crying. Are they hot? No, they aren't.

Are they cold? No, they aren't cold.

Look! Apples. Can the babies eat apples? Yes. What a good idea!

Look, they're hungry. Yes, they like apples.

They're happy now and we're happy too.

items.scene: This is a perfect bike for children aged 7 to 10. It has got big wheels. You can ride it on grass or sand, so take it to the beach or park. Scooters are really good fun. This scooter is fast and easy to ride. It has two small wheels. It is available in pink, green or blue. Are you or your friend learning to skate? These skates have four wheels on each skate, so they are easy and safe for new skaters. They look fantastic, too! This swing is perfect for fun in your garden. Two children can play together as there are two swings. The seats are blue and yellow.

items.title: Unit 3 · Lesson 1 story
items.storyText:
I can skate. I can swim. And I can skateboard.

But I can't ride a bike. Can you teach me please, Grandpa? Yes, of course.

I'm scared, Grandpa. Be brave. I'm here, behind you.

Grandpa. Are you there? Yes, I'm here. Don't stop!

I can't do this. I can't ride a bike. Are you still there? Tim!

Look. You can ride a bike now! Wow! Thanks Grandpa!

items.storySpeech:
Tim: I can skate. I can swim. And I can skateboard.

Tim: But I can't ride a bike. Can you teach me please, Grandpa?

Grandpa: Yes, of course.

Tim: I'm scared, Grandpa.

Grandpa: Be brave. I'm here, behind you.

Tim: Grandpa. Are you there?

Grandpa: Yes, I'm here. Don't stop!

Tim: I can't do this. I can't ride a bike. Are you still there?

Grandpa: Tim!

Grandpa: Look. You can ride a bike now!

Tim: Wow! Thanks Grandpa!

These skates have four wheels on each skate, so they are easy and safe for new skaters. They look fantastic, too! This swing is perfect for fun in your garden. items.scene: One pizza and one banana milkshake, please. We haven't got much food now. Sorry, it's late. Have you got tomatoes? No, sorry. We haven't got tomatoes now. Have you got chicken? Or what about olives? No, we haven't got chicken. And we haven't got olives. You're too late. Oh no! And my milkshake? Have you got bananas? Yes, we've got lots of bananas. Oh good! One banana milkshake and one banana pizza, please! A banana pizza?! Are you sure? Yes, please. Look! I've got a banana pizza! It's my new favourite!

items.storyText:
Have you got a milkshake, Rosy? Yes, I have.

Where's Billy? He's behind the tree.

Has he got a cheese sandwich? No, he hasn't. And he hasn't got his salad.

Here you are, Billy. Thank you.

Billy. Do you like the food? Well … they like the food.

Sorry, Mum. Naughty birds! Don't worry. We've got more food.

Or what about olives? No, we haven't got chicken. And we haven't got olives. You're too late. Oh no! And my milkshake? Have you got bananas? Yes, we've got lots of bananas. Oh good! In the computer room, the pupils can study English, music, maths and science. They do art here too. They can draw and colour pictures with the computer. The computers also help the pupils to read and write. In Primary 2, the children come to the computer room every Tuesday and Thursday. Everyone likes these lessons.

The computers also help the pupils to read and write. In Primary 2, the children come to the computer room every Tuesday and Thursday. Everyone likes these lessons.

items.title: Unit 5 · Lesson 1 story
items.storyText:
What have we got on Monday? We've got English. Then we've got maths.

When have we got PE? We've got PE on Thursday.

On Thursday. Don't forget these. Oh yes. Our PE bags.

It's time for football. Put on your PE clothes now.

Oh no! This is Rosy's bag. I can't wear these clothes. I can't play football now!

You can wear their clothes, Tim. Thank you very much!

items.title: Unit 5 · We've got English!
items.scene: At our school we've got a big computer room. We've got 12 computers in the room, one for every pupil. The computers have got headphones, so the pupils can listen and speak. In the computer room, the pupils can study English, music, maths and science. They do art here too. They can draw and colour pictures with the computer. The computers also help the pupils to read and write. In Primary 2, the children come to the computer room every Tuesday and Thursday. Everyone likes these lessons.

After school, I draw and paint pictures. Then I write stories. I put the stories and pictures on my bedroom wall. I'm Luke. After school, I help my mum and dad. Then I listen to my CDs. I sing the songs. I really like music. My name's Sara. I like sport. I go swimming every Monday. I play tennis with my brother every Tuesday. And every Thursday I skate in the park with my sister.

items.title: Unit 6 · Lesson 1 story
items.storyText:
Let's play after school this week, Alice! Good idea! Can you play on Monday?

Sorry, no. I have a music lesson every Monday. How about Tuesday?

I visit my grandma every Tuesday. Wednesday?

Well, I don't have a music lesson. But I help my mum. Thursday?

I go swimming every Thursday. Oh dear.

Hello, girls. Alice can go swimming with us! Thanks, Mum!

Then I write stories. I put the stories and pictures on my bedroom wall. I'm Luke. After school, I help my mum and dad. Then I listen to my CDs. I sing the songs. I really like music. My name's Sara. I like sport. I go swimming every Monday. I play tennis with my brother every Tuesday. And every Thursday I skate in the park with my sister.

storyDialogue.text: I'm Julia. I love art. After school, I draw and paint pictures. Then I write stories. I put the stories and pictures on my bedroom wall.

storyDialogue.speaker: Luke
storyDialogue.text: I'm Luke. After school, I help my mum and dad. Then I listen to my CDs. I sing the songs. I really like music.

storyDialogue.speaker: Sara
storyDialogue.text: My name's Sara. I like sport. I go swimming every Monday. I play tennis with my brother every Tuesday. And every Thursday I skate in the park with my sister.

items.title: Unit 7 · Lesson 1 story
items.storyText:
It's Billy's birthday tomorrow. Let's buy presents. What does he like? He likes trains and cars.

I like these balloons. No. Billy doesn't like balloons. He's scared of balloons.

He likes chocolate. OK.

Billy is asleep now. Put his presents here. It's a surprise! Good idea, Mum.

Mum, Dad. Someone's in the living room!

Oh Billy! It's five o'clock! Thank you for my presents. I'm three now!

Draw and colour a picture on the front of the card. Now open the card. Draw a picture of you with a big smile. Write in the card, 'Dear Mum, Thank you for everything you do for me.' Then write your name. Give the card to your mum.

items.scene: My name's Ruby. This is my day. And this is my mum's day. In the morning, I get up at seven o'clock. I get dressed. I have breakfast — cereal, bread and milk. Then I go to school at eight o'clock. I go to school by bus. I take my coat, my school bag and my lunch box. Our school bus is blue. My mum's a doctor. She starts work at six o'clock, so I don't see her in the morning. She goes home at two o'clock and she cooks dinner. I see my mum in the afternoon and the evening.

items.storyText: My name's Ruby. This is my day. And this is my mum's day. In the morning, I get up at seven o'clock. I get dressed. I have breakfast — cereal, bread and milk. Then I go to school at eight o'clock. I go to school by bus. I take my coat, my school bag and my lunch box. Our school bus is blue. My mum's a doctor. She starts work at six o'clock, so I don't see her in the morning. She goes home at two o'clock and she cooks dinner. I see my mum in the afternoon and the evening.

items.title: Unit 8 · Lesson 1 story
items.storyText:
Let's listen to music. Sorry, we can't. My dad's asleep.

Asleep? Yes. He's a doctor. He works at night.

He goes to bed at eleven o'clock in the morning. He gets up at seven o'clock.

Hello girls. What's the time? It's seven o'clock.

Can we listen to music now? Sorry, we can't. My brother has dinner at seven o'clock. Then he goes to bed.

Girls. You can listen to music. Put on these headphones. Thanks, Mum!

items.title: Unit 8 · What's the time?
items.scene: My name's Ruby. This is my day. And this is my mum's day. In the morning, I get up at seven o'clock. I get dressed. I have breakfast — cereal, bread and milk. Then I go to school at eight o'clock. I go to school by bus. I take my coat, my school bag and my lunch box. Our school bus is blue. My mum's a doctor. She starts work at six o'clock, so I don't see her in the morning. She goes home at two o'clock and she cooks dinner. I see my mum in the afternoon and the evening.

items.title: Unit 9 · Lesson 1 story
items.storyText:
My dad's a policeman.

Where does he work? He works in a police station.

Does your grandma work? No, she doesn't.

Does your mum work? Yes, she does. She works in a shop.

There are lots of cakes here, Tim. Yes, I know. My mum works in a cake shop!

Have a cake, boys. Oh, thank you. Fantastic!

items.title: Unit 9 · Where does she work?
items.scene: I'm at the zoo with Molly. Molly works at the zoo. She looks after the big animals: elephants, giraffes, lions and tigers. Molly says, 'My favourite animals are the elephants. At the moment we've got six elephants at the zoo. Two of the elephants are babies. They're very cute.' Molly gets up every day at six o'clock. She starts work at seven o'clock. items.title: Unit 10 · Lesson 1 story
items.storyText:
Let's walk to the shops. What's the weather like? It's sunny.

Don't put on your coat, Billy. It's hot today. Children, put on your sun hats, please.

Oh no. It's windy. My hat! Catch it!

Oh no! Now it's raining. And we haven't got our umbrellas! Let's go home.

Quick, Grandpa. Open the door, please. Where's the key? Oh no, I haven't got the key!

Oh! Agh! Oh no, you're all wet!

items.scene: At the airport, planes come and planes go. Where are they going? I don't always know. There are lots of people. Some are short, some are tall. Adults and children, I can't count them all. They've got red coats, green coats, yellow coats, blue. They've got long hair, short hair, and curly hair too. I look through the window. Planes go up, planes go down. Some are not moving. Some are turning around. The plane is here now. It's half past two. And here come my cousins, my aunt and my uncle too.

items.title: Unit 11 · Lesson 1 story
items.storyText:
What time is it, Grandma? It's four o'clock. Look, here's the train!

Oh no. There are lots of people. Where are my aunt and my cousins?

We can't see you. What are you wearing? I'm wearing a blue skirt and a red scarf.

And Joe. What's he wearing? He's wearing jeans and a yellow shirt.

And Milly. What's she wearing? She's wearing red trousers and black boots.

Here they are! Hello and welcome!

items.title: Unit 11 · What are you wearing?
items.scene: At the airport, planes come and planes go. Where are they going? I don't always know. There are lots of people. Some are short, some are tall. Adults and children, I can't count them all. They've got red coats, green coats, yellow coats, blue. They've got long hair, short hair, and curly hair too. I look through the window. Planes go up, planes go down. Some are not moving. Some are turning around. The plane is here now. It's half past two. And here come my cousins, my aunt and my uncle too.

We're watching a video of our wedding. Can we watch too? OK.

Look. The band is playing music. And I'm dancing with my friends.

Look at Grandma. What's she doing? She's eating the wedding cake.

Look at Mum and Aunt Jane. They're talking.

Look at the little baby. It's you, Milly. Oh, I'm so little. And now I'm ten!

Everyone is singing and talking. And you're sleeping!

items.title: Unit 12 · You're sleeping!
items.scene: Dear Hannah, How are you? We're very well. We're getting ready for our summer party. All our family and friends are coming. My brother and I are helping Mum and Dad. We're cooking and cleaning the flat together. Look at this photo. I am with my mum and aunt, Lola. We're choosing party dresses. I like the green and white dress. Look at this. We all like the yellow invitations with purple letters. They're pretty and fun. What do you think? And here, we're choosing party cakes. My brother likes the little cakes. I like the big chocolate cake. I will send photos of the party soon. Love from Bella.

items.title: Unit 13 · Look at all the animals!
items.scene: Dear Parents, We are happy to say that there is a trip to Apple Farm for all the children in Class 2S. The trip is on Wednesday. On this trip, the children learn about farm life and have fun in the open air. There are lots of animals on the farm. In the morning, the children can feed the hens and the ducks. They can also see the cows, horses and goats. The farmer, Mr James, is very friendly. He teaches the children about life on the farm and about where food comes from. The children can also ride in his big tractor. This is always very popular. We are travelling by school bus. The coach goes at 9 o'clock, so please don't be late. Please bring lunch boxes and drinks. Also bring boots, as the farm can be muddy! It is also sunny at the farm, so bring a sun hat too. Here are some photos of last year's trip. Best wishes, Mrs Evans, Class Teacher (Class 2S).

items.storyText: Dear Parents, We are happy to say that there is a trip to Apple Farm for all the children in Class 2S. The trip is on Wednesday. On this trip, the children learn about farm life and have fun in the open air. There are lots of animals on the farm. In the morning, the children can feed the hens and the ducks. They can also see the cows, horses and goats. The farmer, Mr James, is very friendly. He teaches the children about life on the farm and about where food comes from. The children can also ride in his big tractor. This is always very popular. We are travelling by school bus. The coach goes at 9 o'clock, so please don't be late. Please bring lunch boxes and drinks. Also bring boots, as the farm can be muddy! It is also sunny at the farm, so bring a sun hat too. Here are some photos of last year's trip. Best wishes, Mrs Evans, Class Teacher (Class 2S).

items.title: Unit 13 · Lesson 1 story
items.storyText:
Wow! Look at all the animals, Billy.

Look. This cow is bigger than that cow. Yes. It's the mummy cow.

And this sheep is smaller than that sheep. That's right. It's a baby sheep.

Look. A baby donkey and a mummy donkey. That's right, Billy.

Look at that goat. It's bigger than the other goats. Is it a daddy goat?

No. It's a naughty baby goat!

items.title: Unit 13 · Look at all the animals!
items.scene: Dear Parents, We are happy to say that there is a trip to Apple Farm for all the children in Class 2S. The trip is on Wednesday. On this trip, the children learn about farm life and have fun in the open air. There are lots of animals on the farm. In the morning, the children can feed the hens and the ducks. They can also see the cows, horses and goats. The farmer, Mr James, is very friendly. He teaches the children about life on the farm and about where food comes from. The children can also ride in his big tractor. This is always very popular. We are travelling by school bus. The coach goes at 9 o'clock, so please don't be late. Please bring lunch boxes and drinks. Also bring boots, as the farm can be muddy! It is also sunny at the farm, so bring a sun hat too. Here are some photos of last year's trip. Best wishes, Mrs Evans, Class Teacher (Class 2S).

items.scene: Class 2L play was a great success! By Lucy Grant (2L). This year, Class 2L's play was Vet Story. The play was in our classroom on Tuesday morning. I was the vet in the play. Jack and Ruby were ill animals. Jack was a rabbit and Ruby was a cat. My costume was a vet's white coat. Jack's was a fluffy tail and big rabbit ears. Ruby's costume was a big cat's head. In the story, the rabbit was scared of the vet, but in the end he was very brave. The cat was very old and tired, but in the end it was happy and well. The play was lots of fun. Our families were very happy and proud of us. Thank you to our English teacher, Miss Green, for her work. And thank you to our mums and dads for the costumes. Primary 2 was brilliant. We are really looking forward to Primary 3!

items.storyText: Class 2L play was a great success! By Lucy Grant (2L). This year, Class 2L's play was Vet Story. The play was in our classroom on Tuesday morning. I was the vet in the play. Jack and Ruby were ill animals. Jack was a rabbit and Ruby was a cat. My costume was a vet's white coat. Jack's was a fluffy tail and big rabbit ears. Ruby's costume was a big cat's head. In the story, the rabbit was scared of the vet, but in the end he was very brave. The cat was very old and tired, but in the end it was happy and well. The play was lots of fun. Our families were very happy and proud of us. Thank you to our English teacher, Miss Green, for her work. And thank you to our mums and dads for the costumes. Primary 2 was brilliant. We are really looking forward to Primary 3!

items.storyText:
Look at the photos on the fridge.

Look. We were in the park. You were kind, Tim. The babies weren't sad. They were just hungry.

We were outside. We were very wet. Mum wasn't wet. It was dry in the flat!

Look at this one. It was Billy's birthday. He was very naughty.

Look. These ducks were naughty. And this goat was naughty too.

I was naughty then. But I'm not naughty now. I'm a big boy now. Yes, you're very good now!

items.scene: Class 2L play was a great success! By Lucy Grant (2L). This year, Class 2L's play was Vet Story. The play was in our classroom on Tuesday morning. I was the vet in the play. Jack and Ruby were ill animals. Jack was a rabbit and Ruby was a cat. My costume was a vet's white coat. Jack's was a fluffy tail and big rabbit ears. Ruby's costume was a big cat's head. In the story, the rabbit was scared of the vet, but in the end he was very brave. The cat was very old and tired, but in the end it was happy and well. The play was lots of fun. Our families were very happy and proud of us. Thank you to our English teacher, Miss Green, for her work. And thank you to our mums and dads for the costumes. Primary 2 was brilliant. We are really looking forward to Primary 3!

items.scene: Suzy is a fairground horse. She is behind a red horse and in front of a blue horse. She goes round and round every day. But Suzy isn't happy. 'I want to run in the fields,' she says. 'I want to eat the green grass. I want to be a real horse!' The next day Suzy moves her head. She moves her tail. 'Hurrah!' says Suzy. 'I'm a real horse now!' Suzy runs to the field. She eats the green grass. She drinks the fresh water. She is very, very happy. But that night, Suzy isn't happy. She's cold. She's wet. And she's scared. 'I miss my friends,' she says. 'I miss the red horse and the blue horse.' In the morning, Suzy says goodbye to the green grass. She says goodbye to the fresh water. Suzy goes back to the fairground. 'I'm a happy horse,' she says. 'I can go round and round every day with my friends, the red horse and the blue horse.'

items.storyText:
Tell me about school today. Was it good? Oh yes. It was great!

It was the school prize-giving. We were late. Hurry up!

There weren't any children in the classroom. But there were some teachers. Where's the prize-giving?

The prize-giving was in the playground. Look! Lots of men, women and children.

There was a prize for English. The prize goes to …

Rosy and Tim! Well done! We were the winners! It was a great day!

items.scene: Suzy is a fairground horse. She is behind a red horse and in front of a blue horse. She goes round and round every day. But Suzy isn't happy. 'I want to run in the fields,' she says. 'I want to eat the green grass. I want to be a real horse!' The next day Suzy moves her head. She moves her tail. 'Hurrah!' says Suzy. 'I'm a real horse now!' Suzy runs to the field. She eats the green grass. She drinks the fresh water. She is very, very happy. But that night, Suzy isn't happy. She's cold. She's wet. And she's scared. 'I miss my friends,' she says. 'I miss the red horse and the blue horse.' In the morning, Suzy says goodbye to the green grass. She says goodbye to the fresh water. Suzy goes back to the fairground. 'I'm a happy horse,' she says. 'I can go round and round every day with my friends, the red horse and the blue horse.'

'I want to eat the green grass. I want to be a real horse!' The next day Suzy moves her head. She moves her tail. 'Hurrah!' says Suzy. 'I'm a real horse now!' Suzy runs to the field. She eats the green grass. She drinks the fresh water. She is very, very happy. But that night, Suzy isn't happy. She's cold. She's wet. And she's scared. 'I miss my friends,' she says. 'I miss the red horse and the blue horse.' In the morning, Suzy says goodbye to the green grass. She says goodbye to the fresh water. Suzy goes back to the fairground. 'I'm a happy horse,' she says. 'I can go round and round every day with my friends, the red horse and the blue horse.'
